about.headline: So far, I've worked on
about.lede: Developer at Agrifence and master's student in Computer Engineering at FURG. By day I turn raw GPS from agricultural machinery into something a farmer can act on; the rest of the time I research smart contracts and distributed systems, mostly how to make randomness on a public blockchain fair enough to run a lottery on.
about.whyProblems: This blog is where I write about the problem behind the code: the assumptions that seemed obvious until production proved them wrong, what it takes to select a fair winner on a public blockchain, and the shortcuts whose cost only showed up months later.
about.whyProjects: It's also where the projects I haven't built yet live. Some will turn into posts, some into repos, some will stay ideas, but they'll be public either way.

whoami.title: Life is not a mystery to be solved, but an experience to be lived.
whoami.paragraph1: I saw this quote in the movie Dune and thought a lot about it. I believe that many times we turn our insignificance into a form of martyrdom and doubt, when in reality things should be simpler than they actually are.
whoami.paragraph2: You and I are not mere candidates for a place in heaven. If you always live thinking about a future reward, you end up forgetting to live in the present and forgetting who you are.
whoami.paragraph3: According to Jean-Paul Sartre, existence precedes essence. This means that human beings have no predetermined nature. You create your own nature through your actions and choices. Therefore, this question has no correct answer. The responsibilities you take on and the choices you make throughout your life determine who you are.
whoami.paragraph4: Today you might be a programmer, a student, a professional... However, tomorrow you might be a completely different person — it all depends on you.

about.description: I believe that building in public is the best way to grow. I created this portfolio and blog to share ideas, projects, and lessons learned along the journey.
about.community: If you're here, you're already part of this community.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.subtitle: The basics about this place, in a few lines.

items.a: It's my portfolio and my blog in one place. On one side, what I've built and the stack I work with; on the other, writing about engineering, infrastructure and the decisions behind the projects — including the mistakes, which usually teach more than the wins.

items.q: Do I have to pay for anything?
items.a: No. Everything here is free: no paywall, no reading limit, no ads. You don't even need an account to read.

Sharing a post with someone who'd enjoy it already helps a lot. If you'd like to support it financially, you can buy me a coffee via PIX, card or crypto — it covers hosting and the time spent writing. Pointing out a mistake in a post counts for a lot too.

items.q: What do I get by subscribing to the newsletter?
items.a: An email when a new post goes out, and nothing else. No spam, no list selling, no marketing blasts. The unsubscribe link is in every message and works in one click.
An open space for anyone passing by to leave a short note. No theme and no rules beyond common sense: a hello, a topic suggestion, or just marking that you were here.

items.q: Do I need an account to comment?
items.a: Not to read. To comment or like, yes — signing in with Google, GitHub, or email and password. The account only exists to keep spam out and the conversation accountable; I don't use your data for anything else.
It is. The whole site, the infrastructure and the workers are public on GitHub. If you want to understand how a piece of it works, or reuse something, just browse the repository.

cookieBanner.safeExperience: We use cookies to provide a safer, more personalized browsing experience.

whatAreCookies.title: What are cookies?
whatAreCookies.body: Cookies are small text files stored on your device when you visit a website. They are widely used to make websites work more efficiently and to provide information to site owners.

essential.title: 1. Essential cookies
essential.body: These cookies are necessary for the basic operation of the website. They include cookies that allow you to sign in to secure areas or use core functionality. Without them, requested services cannot be provided.

performance.title: 2. Performance cookies
performance.body: These cookies collect information about how visitors use the website — such as the pages visited most often or whether they encounter error messages. They do not collect information that personally identifies a visitor.

functionality.title: 3. Functionality cookies
functionality.body: These cookies allow the website to remember your choices, such as language or region, and provide enhanced, more personalized features. The information collected can be anonymized and cannot track browsing activity on other websites.

targeting.title: 4. Targeting cookies
targeting.body: These cookies are used to present more relevant content and can help limit how many times you see an advertisement, as well as measure the effectiveness of campaigns.

manage.title: 5. How to manage cookies
manage.body: Most browsers allow you to control cookies through preference settings. Limiting cookies may affect your browsing experience and prevent the website from remembering personalized settings.
